input.subject: Job update needed – Lock repair, Flat 23, 155 Willowmere Road (R/PM022-1)
input.body:
Dear Oliver,

Re: Front door lock repair – Flat 23, 155 Willowmere Road, Alderwick, ZZ5 2ZZ (ref R/PM022-1)

We can see you called the tenant on 18/11 to say you were on your way with two locks, but we have no job report on our system yet. Please could you reply today with what happened at the visit:

- Did you attend, and on what date?
- Was the lock repaired or replaced (and what was fitted), or is the job still outstanding?
- If more work is needed, what is it and what is the estimated cost?

Please don't carry out or invoice any further work beyond the original repair until we confirm landlord approval.

Many thanks,
Donna
Maintenance team, Northbridge Lettings

input.subject: Your front door lock – Flat 23, 155 Willowmere Road (R/PM022-1)
input.body:
Dear Amelia,

Re: Front door lock repair – Flat 23, 155 Willowmere Road, Alderwick, ZZ5 2ZZ (ref R/PM022-1)

We are checking on the lock repair. Could you let us know whether the locksmith, Oliver, came to the flat on 18 November, and whether your front door lock now works properly?

If the door ever won't lock or won't open, please call us straight away so we can arrange urgent attendance.

Kind regards,
Donna
Maintenance team, Northbridge Lettings

data.reasoning:
The contractor was supposedly on the way the 18th but there's no confirmation of completed work by the 19th, so I need to follow up directly. The contact details are murky though—there's a name, Oliver Sawyer, and a phone number, but it's unclear whether that's actually the contractor or the tenant, and there's also conflicting info with another name, Maya, plus a scheduling discrepancy between a 14:30 time and an event logged at 15:55.

There's also no record of landlord approval for what may be a lock replacement, and since the lock is still functioning and not a security risk, this isn't an emergency. My plan is to message the contractor for a job status update and message the tenant to confirm whether the visit happened and the lock's current state, holding the contractor task for a day. I'll flag the missing approval as a risk to check against any future invoice rather than escalating now, keeping the primary action as requesting info via email for both the contractor and tenant.

result.summary: The front door lock is stiff but still locks and opens, so the property is secure and this isn't an emergency. On 18/11 the locksmith told the tenant he was on his way with two locks. By 19/11 nothing had been recorded about the visit, and nothing has come in since. I've emailed the locksmith and the tenant asking what happened, and put the ticket on hold with a chase due in 1 day. I haven't moved the stage because there's no proof the work was done.

There are no landlord approvals, holds or attachments on file.
